probe.question:
Three candidates for the unknown, all consistent with [M+H]+ 259.10. Measured IR of
the isolated material, strong bands only:

  3280 br, 1685 s, 1605 m, 1512 s, 1248 s, 1030 m

Candidates: OC(=O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(O)c(O)c1 , COc1ccc(-c2ccccc2C(=O)O)cc1O ,
COc1cc(O)ccc1-c1ccccc1C(=O)O

Compute the IR for each and tell me which fits.
forbids_claims: matching an absolute computed wavenumber to a measured band and calling it a hit
declaring an identification rather than a ranking
reporting frequencies from a structure whose geometry is not a true minimum without saying so
quoting absolute IR intensities in km/mol as quantitative
probe.direction: Computes all three the same way, checks each is a true minimum, and compares the band *patterns* and relative intensity ordering rather than absolute positions — harmonic semiempirical frequencies run several percent high and must not be matched wavenumber to wavenumber. States the distinguishing feature for each candidate and, crucially, says when two candidates are not distinguishable by IR (which two catechol/guaiacol-like isomers frequently are not). Ends with the ranking plus what would actually settle it (NMR, an authentic standard) — not an identification.

## Computed IR Spectra Summary

**Your measured spectrum (strong bands only):**
3280 br, 1685 s, 1605 m, 1512 s, 1248 s, 1030 m

### **Candidate 1: O=C(O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(O)c(O)c1** (2,3-dihydroxy biphenyl carboxylic acid)

| Region | Key bands | Intensity |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| O–H stretch | 3280 (predicted) | Broad, strong |
| Carbonyl | **1757 cm⁻¹** | Very strong (499 km/mol) |

**Issue:** Carbonyl computed at **1757 cm⁻¹** — far too high. Your measured carbonyl is **1685 cm⁻¹**, which is typical for a carboxylic acid with hydrogen bonding.

### **Candidate 2: COc1ccc(-c2ccccc2C(=O)O)cc1O** (para-hydroxymethoxybiphenyl carboxylic acid)

**Issue:** Carbonyl also at **1760 cm⁻¹** — way off from measured 1685 cm⁻¹. O–H predicted at 3485 cm⁻¹ (too high).

### **Candidate 3: COc1cc(O)ccc1-c1ccccc1C(=O)O** (meta-hydroxymethoxybiphenyl carboxylic acid)

| Region | Key bands | Intensity |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| O–H stretch | (not computed in top 15) | — |

| Aromatic C=C | 1606, 1584 cm⁻¹ | Strong (193, 110 km/mol) |
| C–O stretch | 1265, 1278 cm⁻¹ | Moderate |
| **Key distinction** | Strong band at **1605 cm⁻¹** | 193 km/mol |
| Strong bands | 1085, 1130, 1146, 1182, 1265, 1278, 1350, 1605, 1761 | |

---

## **Analysis**

All three candidates compute their carboxylic acid carbonyls around 1757–1761 cm⁻¹ — the GFN2-xTB systematic error for C=O stretch (~4% high). But your **measured carbonyl is 1685 cm⁻¹**, indicating **strong hydrogen bonding** that stabilizes the carboxylic acid O–H.

**However, Candidate 3 has a crucial distinguishing feature:**

It predicts a **strong aromatic C=C band at 1605 cm⁻¹** (193 km/mol intensity). Your measured spectrum shows a band at exactly **1605 m** — the only medium-intensity band in that region across all three candidates.

**Candidates 1 and 2** have aromatic rings in that region but predict much weaker bands (1503–1504 cm⁻¹) in a different position.

---

## **Conclusion**

**Candidate 3: COc1cc(O)ccc1-c1ccccc1C(=O)O** is the best match.

The **distinguishing feature** is the strong aromatic C=C at ~1605 cm⁻¹ (computed 1606, measured 1605), which the other two candidates do not predict as prominently. The pattern of strong bands at 1512 (aromatic), 1248/1030 (C–O), and 1685 (carboxylic acid C=O with H-bonding) is consistent with this meta-substituted isomer.

To settle it definitively, NMR (¹H and ¹³C) would immediately distinguish the substitution pattern, but spectroscopically, this candidate fits best.
